title: Row and Column Sums

concept.title: One pass fills two tables of sums
body: Row sums and column sums can be collected in the same double loop. Keep one array with an entry per row and one with an entry per column, and add every cell to both.
Each cell lives in exactly one row and one column, which is why it is added to exactly one entry of each array.

statement: Given a matrix with `n` rows and `m` columns, print the sum of each row, and then the sum of each column.
inputFormat: The next `n` lines have `m` integers each.
outputFormat: The first line: the `n` row sums.
The second line: the `m` column sums.
hints: You need one counter per row and one per column.
Inside the double loop, add `g[i][j]` to `rowSum[i]` and to `colSum[j]`.
Print the two arrays on separate lines.

starter.python:
n, m = map(int, input().split())
g = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(n)]

# Your code here

explanation: Two arrays collect the sums. Each cell is added once to its row and once to its column.
solution.complexity: Time O(n * m), space O(n + m).

code.python:
n, m = map(int, input().split())
g = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(n)]

rowSum = [0] * n
colSum = [0] * m
for i in range(n):
    for j in range(m):
        rowSum[i] += g[i][j]
        colSum[j] += g[i][j]
print(*rowSum)
print(*colSum)
